I wrote the Markdown renderer in `src/markdown.js`, exporting `render(markdown)`. The one public smoke test passes (`node --test`: 1 pass, 0 fail). I haven't run any other tests, and the hidden suite will be the real check.

I also ran a handful of ad-hoc samples that covered:
- headings, emphasis and strong
- code spans and fenced code blocks
- links and images
- blockquotes and thematic breaks
- tight lists, loose lists, ordered lists with `start`, and hard breaks

All of them produced the expected CommonMark-style HTML. Raw HTML comes out escaped as text. `PROVENANCE.json` is `[]` because nothing external was reused.

Beyond the spec, I also added setext headings, indented code blocks, hard line breaks, and a few HTML entities (`&`, `©` and numeric ones).

One of my earlier shell commands hung waiting for input, and I couldn't stop it. It may still show up as a background task until its timeout. It doesn't affect the code.
